# SK9098 — An arrangement was reverted because it produced new diagnostics

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

This is a Skala bug; the file was left untouched. Re-binding the rewritten document produced a compiler diagnostic it did not have before — or the re-bind itself threw and could not answer whether the rewrite was safe — so nothing was written and a reproduction was dropped under `.skala/crash/`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | error |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Safety layer 2 (docs/plan/06 § "Safety"): a rewrite that cannot prove its precondition does not run, and "it looked right" is not a proof. The two refusals share this id because they are one decision — the layer either answers "no new diagnostics" or it does not answer at all, and in both cases the arrangement is discarded. `CrashRefusal` in the reproduction says which of the two it was: `DiagnosticDelta` or `RebindThrew`.

## When it does not fire

None. A finding here is a bug in Skala. ⚠ It is not a safety net that is always present: under `--arrange=syntactic` there is no compilation to re-bind against, so the layer does not run and this diagnostic cannot fire.
